text:
alex: heads-up — saw steady KV "memory growth" after a Llama -> Mistral handoff in the long-context test (rope_scale=2.5). looks like pages aren't being reclaimed when kernel switches.
mei: can you paste the repro and perf numbers? quick sanity check: is this on dedicated infra or local dev box?
alex: dedicated-staging (gd-rt-12). repro is short: run longctx harness with mixed models, sequence length 32->4096, enable kernel_autoswitch. after ~800 requests, gpu mem used by runtime + kv grows ~200MB and doesn't drop.
alex: snippet of the harness command:

```
./run_longctx.sh --models "llama-2-13b:mistral-7b:qwen-7b" --rope-scale 2.5 --kernel-autoswitch true --iters 1000 --batch 1
```

rik: ugh. sounds like the kernel selection path is leaving KV pages allocated under the old kernel's page format. when we switch to MQA kernels we change page header layout; free path expects header version X but gets Y so they end up on a different freelist.
mei: do we have logs from kernel_switch? any event ids from the runtime?
alex: yea, runtime logs show these entries (condensed):

```
[2025-11-04T09:12:34Z] kernel_switch: model=llama-2-13b kernel=LLAMA_FAST(v1)->LLAMA_MQA(v2)
[2025-11-04T09:12:35Z] kv_alloc: page_id=0x7f8a3b00 size=64k slab=3
[2025-11-04T09:12:35Z] kv_free: page_id=0x7f8a3b00 freelist=LLAMA_FAST_v1
[2025-11-04T09:12:36Z] kernel_switch: model=mistral-7b kernel=MISTRAL_GQA(v1)
[2025-11-04T09:12:36Z] kv_alloc: page_id=0x7f8a3b40 size=64k slab=4
[2025-11-04T09:12:36Z] kv_free: page_id=0x7f8a3b00 freelist=MISTRAL_GQA_v1
```

alex: see the free goes to a different freelist tag. that mismatch is suspicious.
perf-bot: profile snapshot attached (summary): wall_time=00:12:23, kv_total_pages=472, kv_orphan_pages=34, avg_kv_page_residency=2.3s, tail_alloc_latency=18ms
samir: hypothesis: freelist tag is computed from kernel type + quantization mode. when kernel switches we don't normalize tag for pages already in use, so pages freed later land on the wrong freelist and aren't considered by reuse hot path which looks up freelist by current kernel tag.
mei: interesting — that explains slow reuse and why memory keeps growing (we keep allocating fresh pages instead of reusing). can you repro with a forced forced_eviction? how does cache behave if we call kv_sweep manually?
alex: manual kv_sweep reduces memory by ~120MB but leaves ~80MB orphaned pages. sweep logs:

```
kv_sweep: reclaimed=180 pages (11.25MB)
kv_orphan_fix_attempt: scanned=1200 pages, relocated=22
```

rik: relocation code currently compares header.version == current.kernel_version before accepting. we need to add a compatibility path that can reinterpret older headers and convert them lazily on reuse.
samir: another angle: batching heuristics. when we autoswitch kernel mid-batch, some requests get processed under kernel A and others under kernel B but share KV lifespan. we might end up with mixed-format blocks in the same slab which the allocator wasn't designed for.
mei: can we reproduce with a smaller loop that forces mid-batch kernel changes? i can try a two-request batch where request1 triggers kernel A, request2 triggers kernel B.
alex: tried that — reproduced in ~30s. logs show mixed-format writes to same slab_id.

```
allocator: slab_id=12 write format=LLAMA_V1 page_offset=0x100
allocator: slab_id=12 write format=MISTRAL_GQA_V1 page_offset=0x200
```

mei: ok patch idea: 1) conservative — refuse kernel switch if KV in-flight count > threshold for same slab; 2) long-term — add header conversion on free path and unify freelist lookup to check multiple compatible tags; 3) shorter-term mitigation — proactively run kv_sweep on kernel_switch events.
rik: i like #3 as quick mitigation. #2 is better but needs careful testing for perf.
samir: also consider changing batching heuristic to prefer kernel-stable batches: if autoswitch predicted, prefer smaller batches until page churn stabilizes.
perf-bot: suggested config tweak: kernel_autoswitch_rate_limit=60s, kv_sweep_on_switch=true
mei: i'll run a canary with kv_sweep_on_switch=true + limit autoswitch to 1/min on staging and rerun longctx harness.
alex: thanks. if canary looks good let's roll to dedicated-staging for 24h and then decide. also worth adding telemetry: count of frees landing on non-current freelists (new metric)
samir: created a tiny PR to add the metric + kv_sweep_on_switch flag. review pls: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/487
mei: quick local run with flag on: result = no steady growth after 2k requests. memory oscillates but returns to baseline after sweep. will post full numbers in ~1h.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/canary -> dedicated-staging (sha: ab12f4c)
alex: great. follow-up items: 1) backlog ticket for freelist compatibility (#RT-2213), 2) batching heuristic change (#RT-2214), 3) telemetry dashboard for orphan frees (#RT-2215). I'll create them after we confirm canary.
mei: dropping raw repro logs to the thread in a bit. short-term looks promising. :thumbsup:
samir: thanks team, good catch — surprised this surfaced only with rope_scale > 2 due to larger KV lifetimes. likely latent bug for mixed quant/memory kernels.
mei: updating participants on the postmortem channel once we have final numbers.
